Resilience is the long-term capacity of a system to deal with change and continue to develop [ 35 ].
Thus, vulnerability is the measure of a system’s fragility with regard to environmental and other threats.

Social resilience has been defined as the ability of human communities to withstand external shocks to their social infrastructure, such as environmental variability or social, economic, and political upheaval [ 58 , 59 ].
Community resilience refers to the capacities and capabilities of a human community to ‘prevent, withstand, or mitigate’ any traumatic event [ 49 , 50 ].
Community capitals are resources of a community that are invested for the collective wellbeing of the entire community.
Ecological resilience can be defined as the buffer capacity of ecosystems to absorb externally caused perturbation, maintain robust functions, and survive systemic shocks [ 6 , 73 ].
When a system develops coping mechanisms with regard to a specific threat, its adaptive capability is termed as specified resilience.
General resilience, on the other hand, is the resilience which a system grows in order to address all sorts of shocks simultaneously.

value: A community is strongly resilient when its economic, social and environmental capitals are all well developed, and weakly resilient when one or none is.
quote: A community is strongly resilient when all three capitals are well developed in it, while it is weakly resilient when only one or no capital is well developed in it, and furthermore, a community is moderately resilient when two capitals are well developed.
